mainTopic: The גמרא on the משנה of the 39 אבות מלאכות: why there is a count, which acts are grouped under each אב, cases of double liability, and why similar מלאכות are counted separately.
overview: The גמרא explains why the משנה gives the number 39: someone who does all of them in one הֶעְלֵם brings a separate חטאת for each one. It explains that זורע comes before חורש because in ארץ ישראל farmers sowed first and then plowed. Then it goes through the list one מלאכה at a time, using ברייתות to group similar acts under one heading: planting-type acts under זורע, digging and furrowing under חורש, all kinds of harvesting under קוצר, and beating flax and stripping cotton under דש. Acts in the same group bring only one חטאת. Some single acts bring two, like pruning when he wants the wood, which is both קוצר and נוטע. Leveling ground counts as בונה in a house and חורש in a field. Digging only for the dirt is פטור, because it is מקלקל. רב פפא and רב אשי argue about knocking dates down with a clod, and רבא and אביי argue whether gathering salt counts as מעמר. Finally, the גמרא asks why זורה, בורר and מרקד are counted separately, and אביי and רבא begin an answer based on the משכן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the משנה give a number?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה states the total count of 39 מלאכות when it lists them anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need the count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה says 'forty minus one' when we could simply count the list ourselves. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists every מלאכה one by one, so adding the total looks unnecessary. The גמרא assumes every word in a משנה teaches something. So the number must carry a legal lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Why do I need it? (asks what a detail adds)

phrases.english: Gemara:
Why do I need the count (of forty minus one)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of the 39 אבות מלאכות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What legal point does the number 39 teach beyond the list itself?

steps.title: The count teaches a separate liability for each labor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the number teaches that someone who does all 39 in one הֶעְלֵם is liable for each one separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The count teaches that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. The number tells us that each of the 39 is a separate prohibition, so each one brings its own חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, sins done in one הֶעְלֵם אֶחָד (one stretch of forgetting) can combine into one חטאת. The count of 39 tells us there are 39 separate units of liability. So even in one stretch of forgetting, a person who did all of them brings 39 קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: One lapse of awareness (one period of forgetting)
Liable for each and every one separately
Sin-offering brought for an unintentional transgression

steps.whatToRemember: The number 39 is not decoration. It sets the maximum number of separate חטאות for one הֶעְלֵם on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole sugya that follows: which acts count as separate מלאכות and which count as the same one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
That if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness —
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The count teaches separate liability for each מלאכה, even when all are done in one הֶעְלֵם.

steps.title: Why is sowing listed before plowing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the order of the משנה: plowing comes before sowing in real life, so חורש should be listed first.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who sows and one who plows.' Since, after all, people plow first, let the משנה teach plowing and then teach sowing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's first two items and asks a question about their order. Farmers plow first and sow afterward, so why does the משנה put זורע first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that the משנה lists the מלאכות in the order of the bread-making process. If so, the list seems to have the first two steps backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all (introduces an obvious premise)

phrases.english: 'One who sows and one who plows.'
Since, after all, people plow first,
let him teach 'plows' and then teach 'sows'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new detail in the משנה: the order of the list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of זורע before חורש in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real farming goes plow, then sow, so the list appears out of order.

steps.title: The משנה follows farming in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The תנא follows the practice in ארץ ישראל, where people sow first and then plow over the seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is standing in ארץ ישראל, where they sow first and then plow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in ארץ ישראל farmers sowed first and then plowed afterward, so the order is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל, a plowing after sowing was used to cover the seeds. The משנה lists the steps in the order that was familiar to its own setting. So the assumption that the list follows the bread-making process still holds.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not deny that people plow before sowing. It means that in ארץ ישראל there was also a plowing after sowing, and the משנה lists that order.

phrases.english: The Tanna is standing in Eretz Yisrael,
where they sow first and then plow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question about the order of the list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since plowing always comes first, the list seems out of order.
steps.terutzMaskana: In ארץ ישראל they sowed and then plowed, and the משנה follows that order.

steps.title: ברייתא: Sowing, pruning, planting, bending and grafting are one labor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that זורע, זומר, נוטע, מבריך and מרכיב all count as one מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: One who sows, prunes, plants, bends a branch into the ground, or grafts — all of them are one labor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that groups five growth-promoting actions together under one heading. This sets up the question of what the ברייתא is coming to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All five actions help a plant grow. So the ברייתא puts them in one family of work rather than treating them as five separate מלאכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Bends a branch into the ground so it takes root
Grafts a branch onto another tree

phrases.english: It was taught: One who sows, and one who prunes, and one who plants,
and one who bends (a branch into the ground), and one who grafts —
all of them are one labor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: which acts fall within the מלאכה of זורע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sowing, pruning, planting, bending and grafting are all one מלאכה.

steps.title: What is the ברייתא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical point the ברייתא is making by calling them one מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters that these acts are 'one labor'. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these acts is forbidden anyway. So the גמרא wants to know what legal difference the grouping makes.

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the practical result of grouping these acts as one מלאכה?

steps.title: Many acts of one labor bring only one sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: Someone who does many acts that all belong to one מלאכה is liable only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: One who does many labors that are of the type of one labor is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the grouping limits liability. Doing several of these acts in one הֶעְלֵם brings only one חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the flip side of רבי יוחנן's rule in step 2. Different אבות bring separate חטאות. But several acts within the same אב count as one.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Of the same type as one labor

steps.whatToRemember: Different אבות מלאכות bring separate חטאות. Many acts inside one אב bring only one.

phrases.english: [This is what it teaches us:]
one who does many labors
of the type of one labor
is liable only once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Several acts within one מלאכה bring only one חטאת.

steps.title: רבי אמי: Pruning is planting; planting, bending and grafting are sowing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי assigns pruning to נוטע, and planting, bending and grafting to זורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא said in the name of רבי חייא בר אשי in the name of רבי אמי: One who prunes is liable for planting; one who plants, bends, or grafts is liable for sowing.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא states the exact heading under which each of these acts is punished. This sets up the גמרא's question about the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said all these acts are one מלאכה. רבי אמי now names the specific label for each one: pruning falls under planting, and the other three fall under sowing.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of / under the heading of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Acha said that Rabbi Chiya bar Ashi said that Rabbi Ami said:
One who prunes is liable for planting,
and one who plants, and one who bends, and one who grafts
is liable for sowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the heading for each act grouped in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זומר → נוטע; נוטע, מבריך, מרכיב → זורע.

steps.title: Only for sowing and not for planting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: could planting, bending and grafting count as sowing but not as planting?
steps.simpleTranslation: For sowing, yes; for planting, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי's wording. These are tree activities, so they look much more like planting than sowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, the statement suggests that a person who plants or grafts a tree is not liable under נוטע. That is very strange, since planting is literally נוטע.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם זוֹרֵעַ אִין, מִשּׁוּם נוֹטֵעַ לָא?
phrases.english: For sowing, yes; for planting, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם זוֹרֵעַ אִין, מִשּׁוּם נוֹטֵעַ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's wording that נוטע, מבריך and מרכיב are liable 'for sowing'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tree-growing acts are obviously planting. Labeling them only as sowing seems backward.

steps.title: Correct the wording: also for sowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the statement: they are liable for planting, and also for sowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: even for sowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. These acts are liable as planting, and they can even be called sowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that נוטע and זורע are one מלאכה on שבת. So an act of planting can be described under either name, and there is no extra liability.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean two חטאות, one for planting and one for sowing. Planting and sowing are the same מלאכה, so the word 'also' only describes it under both names.

phrases.english: Say: even (also) for sowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 9 by rewording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Planting-type acts are liable only as sowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are liable as planting, and also under the name of sowing, since the two are one מלאכה.

steps.title: רב כהנא: Pruning when you want the wood
steps.stepSummary: Someone who prunes and wants the wood is liable twice: once for קוצר and once for נוטע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: One who prunes and needs the wood is liable twice: once for reaping and once for planting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives a case where one action breaks two different מלאכות at once. Cutting off wood he wants is reaping, and helping the tree grow is planting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each result of the act counts on its own. Taking something useful off a growing plant is קוצר, and making the tree grow better is נוטע. Since these are two different אבות, he brings two חטאות.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
One who prunes and needs the wood —
is liable twice:
once for reaping,
and once for planting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on זומר = נוטע and adds a second liability for קוצר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pruning when he needs the wood makes him liable twice: קוצר and נוטע.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Cutting alfalfa
steps.stepSummary: Cutting alfalfa makes a person liable for קוצר and for נוטע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: One who cuts alfalfa is liable twice: once for reaping and once for planting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a parallel case. Cutting alfalfa harvests it, and it also makes the plant grow back stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the pruning case, one cut has two results: harvesting the feed (קוצר) and helping regrowth (נוטע). So there are two separate liabilities.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
One who cuts alfalfa
is liable twice:
once for reaping,
and once for planting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case of one act with two liabilities.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting alfalfa brings liability for קוצר and נוטע.

steps.title: אביי: Cutting beet leaves
steps.stepSummary: Cutting beet leaves makes a person liable for קוצר and for זורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: One who cuts beet leaves is liable twice: once for reaping and once for sowing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a third case of the same pattern. Here the second liability is called זורע instead of נוטע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beets are a vegetable grown from seed, not a tree. So helping them grow back is called sowing rather than planting. The pattern is the same as before: harvest plus regrowth equals two חטאות.
steps.whatToRemember: One act can bring two חטאות when it does two different jobs: harvesting (קוצר) and helping the plant grow (נוטע/זורע). Several acts inside one מלאכה bring only one.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One who cuts beet leaves
is liable twice:
once for reaping,
and once for sowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel case, using זורע for a vegetable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting beet leaves brings liability for קוצר and זורע.

steps.title: Plowing, digging and furrowing are one מלאכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the word חורש from the משנה and brings a ברייתא: plowing, digging and furrowing are all one מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'one who plows.' A ברייתא taught: one who plows, one who digs, and one who makes a furrow have all done one type of מלאכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next מלאכה in the משנה, חורש. It quotes a ברייתא that puts three ground-working actions under this one heading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging and furrowing don't look exactly like plowing, but they all loosen or prepare the ground. So they count as one מלאכה, and doing all three at once (בשגגה) brings only one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Plowing, one of the 39 אבות מלאכה
One single category of forbidden labor

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] And one who plows.
phrases.notes: Quoting the next word in the משנה's list

phrases.english: It was taught: one who plows, one who digs, and one who makes a furrow
all of them are one labor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of זורע and נוטע and moves to the next מלאכה in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plowing, digging and furrowing all count as the single מלאכה of חורש.

steps.title: Removing a mound: building in a house, plowing in a field
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת: removing a mound of earth is בונה if done in a house and חורש if done in a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: If someone had a mound of earth and removed it, in a house he is חייב for building, and in a field he is חייב for plowing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a case where one action counts as a different מלאכה depending on where it happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leveling the floor of a house fixes the building, so it counts as בונה. Leveling a field gets the ground ready for planting, so it counts as חורש. The action is the same, but what it accomplishes decides which מלאכה it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A small mound or bump of earth

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
If he had a mound of earth and removed it,
in the house, he is liable for building;
in the field, he is liable for plowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another way to violate חורש, by leveling the ground.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing a mound is בונה in a house and חורש in a field.

steps.title: Filling a hole: building in a house, plowing in a field
steps.stepSummary: רבא: filling a hole follows the same rule. It is בונה in a house and חורש in a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If someone had a hole and filled it in, in a house he is חייב for building, and in a field for plowing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the matching case to רב ששת's: filling a hole instead of removing a mound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a bump and filling a hole both make the ground level. So רבא applies the same rule: in a house it is בונה, and in a field it is חורש.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he had a hole and filled it in,
in the house, he is liable for building;
in the field, for plowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָיְתָה לוֹ גּוּמָּא וּטְמָמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The parallel case to רב ששת's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Filling a hole is בונה in a house and חורש in a field.

steps.title: Digging a hole only for its dirt is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא: someone who digs a hole on שבת only because he wants the dirt is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: One who digs a hole on שבת and needs only its dirt is exempt for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא gives a case where digging does NOT make a person חייב, because he doesn't want the hole at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, digging is forbidden because a hole is useful for the ground or a building. Here the person only wants the dirt, and the hole is an unwanted side result. So he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Its dirt (the earth dug out of the hole)
Exempt (from a קרבן or Torah punishment)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
One who digs a hole on Shabbat
and needs only its dirt —
is exempt for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After cases that create liability, this gives a digging case with no liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Digging a hole only for the dirt is פטור.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה agrees, because this digging is destructive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that even רבי יהודה, who usually holds a person חייב for מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, would agree here, because his rule covers only constructive acts and this one is destructive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי יהודה, who said that one who does a מלאכה not needed for its own purpose is חייב: that applies only when he is fixing something. This person is damaging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question before anyone asks it: doesn't רבי יהודה disagree with רבי אבא's ruling? It explains why רבי יהודה would agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think רבי אבא's פטור depends on the rule of מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, which רבי יהודה rejects. But the גמרא says this case has a second reason to be פטור: making a pointless hole damages the ground, and a מקלקל (one who damages) is פטור by everyone's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: A מלאכה done for a purpose other than its usual result

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה changed his opinion. He still holds a person חייב for מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. This case is פטור for a separate reason: it is מקלקל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two separate reasons a person can be פטור on שבת: מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, and מקלקל.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who said that a labor not needed for its own sake
one is liable for it —
that applies only when he is fixing;
this one is damaging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי אבא's ruling against a possible challenge from רבי יהודה's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבי יהודה's rule to constructive acts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה would make the digger חייב, because he holds a person חייב for מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה's rule covers only מתקן. Digging an unwanted hole is מקלקל, so everyone agrees it is פטור.

steps.title: All kinds of harvesting are one מלאכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes קוצר from the משנה and brings a ברייתא: reaping, picking grapes, harvesting dates, collecting olives, and gathering figs are all one מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'one who reaps.' It was taught: one who reaps grain, picks grapes, harvests dates, collects olives, or gathers figs has done one type of מלאכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next מלאכה, קוצר, and lists the different harvesting words that all fall under it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each crop has its own word for harvesting, but they are all the same act: removing produce from where it grows. So they all count as קוצר.

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] And one who reaps.
It was taught: one who reaps, one who picks grapes,
and one who harvests dates, and one who collects olives, and one who gathers figs —
all are one labor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from חורש to the next מלאכה in the משנה, קוצר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All types of harvesting count as the single מלאכה of קוצר.

steps.title: Knocking down dates with a clod: two liabilities
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא: someone who throws a clod at a palm tree and knocks down dates is חייב twice, for תולש and for מפרק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Someone who threw a clod of earth at a palm tree and knocked down dates is חייב two קרבנות: one for detaching, and one for separating.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a case where one throw breaks two מלאכות at the same moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knocking the dates off the tree is תולש, a תולדה of קוצר. Knocking them off their cluster is מפרק, a תולדה of דש (threshing), because it separates food from its covering. One action produces two separate results.

keyTerms.meaning: Detaching from where it grows (a תולדה of קוצר)
Separating food from its shell or cluster (a תולדה of דש)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
One who threw a clod of earth at a palm tree
and knocked down dates
is liable for two:
one for detaching,
and one for separating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a specific case involving קוצר, plus a second מלאכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Knocking dates down with a clod makes a person חייב for both תולש and מפרק.

steps.title: רב אשי: this is not the normal way of harvesting
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees: throwing a clod is not the normal way to detach or to separate dates, so the person is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That is not the normal way of detaching, and that is not the normal way of separating.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with רב פפא and says there is no liability at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a person is חייב only for doing a מלאכה the usual way. Nobody normally harvests or separates dates by throwing clods at them. So רב אשי holds that both of רב פפא's liabilities fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not the usual way' (an unusual manner, which makes one פטור)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
That is not the normal way of detaching,
and that is not the normal way of separating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly disagrees with רב פפא's ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both of רב פפא's liabilities.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב פפא ignored that the act is done in an unusual manner (שלא כדרכו), which makes a person פטור.

steps.title: רבא: gathering salt counts as מעמר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes מעמר from the משנה. רבא says someone who gathers salt from salt pools is חייב for מעמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'one who gathers.' רבא said: Someone who gathers salt from salt pools is חייב for gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next מלאכה, מעמר, and רבא says it applies to collecting salt too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעמר means gathering scattered items into a pile where they were produced. רבא holds that salt formed in salt pools counts, just like produce gathered in a field.

keyTerms.meaning: Gathering (piling produce together), one of the 39 מלאכות

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] And one who gathers.
Rava said:
One who gathers salt from salt pools
is liable for gathering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from קוצר to the next מלאכה in the משנה, מעמר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gathering salt from salt pools is מעמר.

steps.title: אביי: gathering applies only to things that grow from the ground
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees: מעמר applies only to things that grow from the ground, and salt does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no gathering except with things that grow from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues with רבא and limits מעמר to plants and produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that the מלאכה of מעמר, by its nature, covers only produce that grows from the ground. Salt is not grown, so collecting it is not מעמר. The גמרא does not give a further reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that grow from the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Each מלאכה has limits. Leveling ground can be בונה or חורש depending on where it happens. Digging only for the dirt is מקלקל and פטור. רב פפא and רב אשי argue whether an unusual way of harvesting creates liability. רבא and אביי argue whether מעמר applies to things that don't grow.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
There is no gathering except with things that grow from the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly disagrees with רבא's ruling about salt.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא extended מעמר beyond גידולי קרקע, but מעמר applies only to things that grow.

steps.title: Threshing, beating flax, and stripping cotton are one labor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes דש from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that דש, מנפץ, and מנפט all count as one מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'and one who threshes.' A ברייתא taught: one who threshes, one who beats flax stalks, and one who strips cotton from its seeds have all done one type of מלאכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next מלאכה in the משנה, which is דש. It brings a ברייתא that groups related activities under it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three actions do the same job. Each one removes the useful part of a plant from the shell or husk around it. So they are not new אבות מלאכה. They all fall under the one category of דש. This follows the same pattern as Step 19, where many kinds of harvesting were grouped under קוצר.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing: separating grain from its husk or stalk
Beating flax to separate the fibers from the hard stalk
Striking or stripping cotton to remove its seeds
'It was taught.' This introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: And one who threshes.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה's list of אבות מלאכה

phrases.english: It was taught: one who threshes, one who beats flax, and one who strips cotton —
are all one labor.
phrases.notes: They are not separate אבות. They all count under דש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next מלאכה in the משנה, following the same pattern as the קוצר ברייתא in Step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דש, מנפץ, and מנפט are a single מלאכה. Each one separates a product from its natural casing.

steps.title: Aren't winnowing, selecting, and sifting the same thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes זורה, בורר, טוחן, and מרקד from the משנה. It asks why זורה, בורר, and מרקד are counted separately when they seem to be the same activity.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה listed: one who winnows, one who selects, one who grinds, and one who sifts. But winnowing is the same as selecting, and that is the same as sifting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's list. It points out that three of the מלאכות seem to be the same action, so why are they counted as three?
steps.deeperAnalysis: זורה, בורר, and מרקד all separate food from waste. The only difference is the method: wind, hand, or sieve. Since the goal is the same, it seems they should be one מלאכה, just like the ברייתא grouped דש, מנפץ, and מנפט together in Step 24. So why does the משנה count them separately to reach its total of 39?

keyTerms.meaning: Winnowing: throwing grain into the wind so the chaff blows away
Selecting: picking waste out from food, or food out from waste
'That is the same as.' This is a formula that challenges something as a repeat

steps.confusionAlert: טוחן is not part of the question. The גמרא only says that זורה, בורר, and מרקד are the same. Grinding is clearly a different action.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question leads to a basic rule about how the 39 מלאכות are counted: the משכן decides what counts as a separate מלאכה, not just whether two actions look alike.

phrases.english: One who winnows, one who selects,
and one who grinds, and one who sifts.
Winnowing is the same as selecting, which is the same as
sifting!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ זוֹרֶה, הַיְינוּ בּוֹרֵר, הַיְינוּ מְרַקֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the next group of מלאכות in the משנה and challenges why they are counted separately, which is the opposite of the grouping in Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of זורה, בורר, and מרקד as three separate אבות מלאכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All three separate food from waste. Activities with the same purpose should count as one מלאכה, so listing them separately looks like needless repetition.

steps.title: אביי and רבא begin their answer from the משכן
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא begin to answer with a principle: anything that was done in the משכן... (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said: any activity that was done in the משכן...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to the question about זורה, בורר, and מרקד. This step only sets up the principle, and the rest of the sentence comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is going to be based on the משכן, because the 39 מלאכות come from the work done to build it. The idea starting here is that if the משכן had separate activities, each one counts as its own מלאכה, even if they look alike. The full rule is finished on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Both of them.' Here it means אביי and רבא said the same thing
The Tabernacle. The 39 מלאכות of שבת come from the work done to build it

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both said:
Any activity that was done in the Mishkan,
phrases.notes: The sentence is not finished. It continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of why זורה, בורר, and מרקד are counted separately
steps.terutzResolutionType: A principle that the משכן decides how the מלאכות are counted. It is only partly stated on this amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Actions that look alike and have the same purpose should count as one מלאכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still developing: activities that were done separately in the משכן each count as their own מלאכה, even if they look similar.
